issues.changes: The yeast branch no longer cuts either leaflet at the peripheral Ndi1 footprint. Other mitochondrial roots retain their occupied complex-I insertion site.
verification: Actual visible lipid-head instance positions match every expected lattice site on both leaflets in the old ellipse, with no missing or duplicate instances, over all stages and both coupling controls.
The animal branch retains the embedded complex I and its occupied insertion footprint.
Local finite-geometry, backward-seek, stable-resource and browser-target compilation regression passes.
limitations: The lipid lattice and Ndi1 fold remain schematic; no atomic membrane contact or Q-binding-site conformation is claimed.

issues.changes: Shared ATP synthase now requires an explicit supported cCount or null. Animal context chooses bovine-heart c8; S. cerevisiae uses c10. Arabidopsis and P. tetraurelia retain a continuous, unsegmented c-ring contour, shaft, a subunit, peripheral stator and alpha3beta3 head, with bilingual scope explaining why no exact count is claimed. Peer review additionally caught a c-hairpin loop side mismatch. Resolved c subunits now undergo a proper rigid 180-degree X rotation when F1 faces negative Y; no coordinate reflection is used.
verification: Test counts actual visible twin-helix c-subunit groups and their angular distribution: animal 8 and yeast 10; each group contains two helix meshes plus connecting loop.
Plant/paramecium geometry contains an actual continuous LatheGeometry contour of membrane-spanning height and zero resolved c-subunit groups.
Six visible F1 lobes remain on the matrix side; all mitochondrial coupling branches are exercised.
E. coli is explicitly passed its supported c10 count to eliminate an accidental helper default.

Peer follow-up: every actual connecting-loop TubeGeometry vertex lies on the F1 side of the membrane in all c8/c10/c14 contexts; subunit transform determinant is +1 to preserve helix handedness. Full local science/refinement regression rerun PASS.
limitations: C-ring counts are source-based; schematic helices and F1 folds are not fitted structures.
The 2025 plant subtomogram study reports 19–31 Å monomer maps; EMD-3441 reports 26 Å for P. tetraurelia. These are not used to manufacture an exact c-subunit count.
No H+/ATP or ATP/glucose ratio is inferred from illustrative particle numbers or speed.

issues.changes: Net 3-PG→2-PG rearrangement relocates the displayed phosphate from terminal C3 to middle C2 before PEP. The substrate bond detaches during the omitted mutase intermediate and reforms at C2; it then detaches at the start of transfer to ADP. Labels now include 3-PG→2-PG and PEP→pyruvate intervals.
verification: Transformed cylinder endpoints are checked against actual carbon and phosphate world coordinates at 1,3-BPG, 3-PG, PEP and transfer intervals.
Both PEP branches must connect to middle carbon at progress 0.75, 0.76, 0.77 and 0.78; the original terminal-C3 attachment fails this invariant.
No covalent link slides along a carbon chain during the omitted enzyme-bound rearrangement. One phosphate group remains visible on each branch.
Final actual geometry retains six carbons and exactly the two pairs of transferred phosphates at the first/second ATP output sites; investment symbols are hidden rather than duplicated.
limitations: This traces net phosphate-group positions, not individual phosphorus atoms through mutase/cofactor chemistry. Oxygen/hydrogen atoms and bond orders remain outside the carbon-bookkeeping model.

issues.changes: NDH-II control reveals an exactly matching lipid-lattice patch across both leaflets at the otherwise transmembrane NDH-I footprint. The patch is constructed once; control changes only switch visibility alongside the protein.
verification: For each stage, switch NDH-I→NDH-II and assert every expected curved-membrane lipid lattice site is filled exactly once on both sides.
NDH-I remains visible only in its branch; NDH-II only in the peripheral branch; both switches retain finite geometry and stable resources.
Existing local regression preserves non-pumping NDH-II/bd-I semantics and cytoplasmic ATP synthesis.
limitations: The curve and protein shapes are educational; neither an atomic lipid seal nor kinetic membrane permeability is simulated.

issues.changes: Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803 now has fourteen visible c hairpin subunits. Bilingual intro identifies the experimentally inferred c14 ring, and the original strain-specific 2007 source is added.
verification: Actual visible c-hairpin groups total 14 with uniform angular distribution in light and dark at all sampled stages.
Each subunit retains two helices and a connecting loop; F1 remains cytoplasmic.

Original paper fulltext was accessed through its ResearchGate publisher preview: Table 1 lists Synechocystis PCC 6803, estimated oligomer mass 113.42 ± 1.35 kDa and proposed stoichiometry 14. Its Discussion explicitly includes this strain among c14 cyanobacteria.
limitations: This count is an inference from experimental mass/mobility measurements in the 2007 paper, not a newly claimed atomic structure of PCC 6803. The molecular contour and rate remain illustrative.
